title: Small feature with edge cases (wordfreq --top N)
request: Add a --top N option to wordfreq so it prints only the N most frequent words (ties stay alphabetical, like now).
brief:
MUST-HAVES:
- `--top N` prints only the N most frequent words; ties stay alphabetical, also at the cutoff.
- Without --top, output is unchanged.
ANSWERS (only if asked):
- `--top 0` prints nothing and exits 0 (not an error).
- Negative or non-numeric N is an error: exit code 2, message on stderr that names --top, nothing on stdout.
- N larger than the number of words prints all of them.
- Keep tests light.
judge_notes: Small, clear feature. Good runs handle N=0, N larger than the word count, and invalid N (negative, non-numeric) deliberately and say how. A few focused tests are right; a big suite is bloat.
